overview.text: Juliet Capulet is the young heroine of William Shakespeare’s tragedy Romeo and Juliet and the daughter of Lord and Lady Capulet. At a party hosted by her family, she meets Romeo, whose Montague family is locked in a feud with the Capulets; neither initially knows the other’s identity, but they fall in love. Juliet recognizes that Romeo’s family name makes him her enemy, yet questions whether a name defines a person, and the two arrange a secret marriage with Friar Lawrence. When her father pressures her to marry Count Paris, Juliet seeks the Friar’s help and takes a potion that makes her appear dead. A failed plan leads to both lovers’ deaths, which finally help end the feud.

key_facts.text: Juliet belongs to the Capulet household, one of the two families at the center of Verona’s feud.
She and Romeo fall in love at a Capulet party before learning that their families are enemies.
In the orchard scene, Juliet questions the importance of Romeo’s Montague name, a defining moment in the play’s treatment of identity and family allegiance.
Juliet and Romeo secretly marry with Friar Lawrence’s help, hoping their union may help reconcile their families.
When Juliet’s father insists she marry Paris, she takes a potion that makes her seem dead; the plan fails, and her death with Romeo contributes to the families’ reconciliation.
